chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and al-Hajjāl, from Thal'abah ibn Maymūn, from Ma'mar ibn 'Uthmān, who said:
I asked Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) about whom upon whom the clothing is obligatory in the expiation of the oath. He said: 'A garment that covers his private parts.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum clothing requirement for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the minimum standard for the garment used in expiating an oath is defined not by material value but by its functional ability to cover the 'awrah. This establishes a practical, modesty-based criterion within Shia fiqh, ensuring the expiation is accessible while maintaining the dignity required for religious obligations. The ruling reflects the broader Islamic principle that acts of worship must fulfill their essential purpose of covering and modesty.
